title: Wide Diamond Isolation Patterns
definition: A tactical structure using wide center backs and attacking midfielders to create 1v1 situations for central strikers via split runs and third-man combinations.
content: This concept describes a specific attacking pattern often seen in 3-2-5 or 3-1-6 structures where the team utilizes a 'wide diamond' shape in the final third. The center backs push wide to create width, while the attacking midfielders position themselves between the wing-backs and the outer center backs. This specific spacing forces the opponent's outer center back to commit to the wide attacker, thereby isolating the central striker (often a channel runner) in a 1v1 situation against the remaining central defender. The system relies heavily on vertical, line-breaking passes and quick third-man combinations to bypass defensive lines. Additionally, split runs are a key feature: one player (e.g., the striker) pins the central defender, while the attacking midfielder drops to receive, allowing the full-back or wing-back to make a high run into the vacated space, or vice versa. This requires high technical proficiency in first-time passing and precise timing of runs to exploit the gaps created by the opponent's defensive commitment to the wide areas.
